project.name: nisshi
project.description: Stateless, Apache Kafka-compatible broker written in Rust with pluggable storage backends (PostgreSQL, libSQL/SQLite, S3/object store, memory); schema-backed topics can be written as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake tables.

nodes.name: mod.rs
nodes.summary: Shared test-support module for nisshi-storage integration tests: defines a shared Error enum wrapping I/O, message, filter-parse, protocol, and storage errors, plus an init_tracing helper that sets up a per-thread tracing subscriber writing to a log file under ../logs/.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Test-only error enum aggregating I/O, generic message, filter-parse, config-parse, protocol, and storage error variants for use across nisshi-storage integration tests.

nodes.name: init_tracing
nodes.summary: Loads .env, then installs a thread-scoped tracing subscriber that writes debug-level logs to a per-test-thread file under ../logs/<crate>/, returning a DefaultGuard to keep it active for the test's duration.

nodes.name: latency.rs
nodes.summary: Implements LatencyIntroducingStorage, a Storage decorator used in tests that injects randomized artificial latency around every backend operation to simulate a slow storage layer.

nodes.name: LatencyIntroducingStorage
nodes.summary: Storage decorator that wraps another backend and sleeps for a randomized duration (seeded RNG) before/after delegating each call, simulating latency for chaos testing.

nodes.name: os.rs
nodes.summary: Small set of `From` conversions between the `object_store` crate's version/metadata types (ETag, ObjectMeta, PutResult) and the crate's own `Version` type used for optimistic-concurrency updates.

nodes.name: consumer.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Kafka embedded consumer group protocol: partition assignor strategies, member metadata/assignment (de)serialization, and the GroupConsumer state machine driving join/sync/heartbeat actions.

nodes.name: ConsumerAssignor
nodes.summary: Trait implemented by each partition assignment strategy (e.g., range, round-robin) used by the consumer group protocol.

nodes.name: Assignor
nodes.summary: Enum wrapper over the built-in partition assignor implementations, dispatching assign() and name lookup to the selected strategy.

nodes.name: MemberMetadata
nodes.summary: Versioned wrapper for a consumer group member's subscription metadata, encoding/decoding the ConsumerProtocolSubscription payload.

nodes.name: ConsumerProtocolSubscription
nodes.summary: Represents the subscription payload a consumer sends when joining a group: subscribed topics, owned partitions, generation id, and rack id.

nodes.name: TopicPartition
nodes.summary: Simple topic-name/partition-id pair used throughout the consumer group assignment protocol.

nodes.name: MemberAssignment
nodes.summary: Versioned wrapper for a consumer group member's partition assignment payload returned by the group leader.

nodes.name: ConsumerProtocolAssignment
nodes.summary: Represents the assigned-partitions payload embedded in a member's assignment, plus optional user data.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Builder for constructing a consumer's join-group protocol metadata, accumulating topics, metadata, and timeout settings before building the final payload.

nodes.name: MemberState
nodes.summary: Tracks a single group member's role (leader/follower/outsider) and current assignment/generation state during a rebalance.

nodes.name: GroupConsumer
nodes.summary: Central consumer group state machine that decides the next protocol action (join, sync, heartbeat, leave) based on member state, timeouts, and errors.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds the final join-group protocol metadata payload (topics, metadata, timeouts) from the accumulated Builder state.

nodes.name: join_protocol
nodes.summary: Selects and encodes the consumer protocol metadata to advertise for a given assignor when joining a group.

nodes.name: join_request
nodes.summary: Assembles the full JoinGroup request for the consumer, combining the protocol name and its encoded metadata.

nodes.name: next_action
nodes.summary: Core decision function of the consumer group state machine: given the current member/group state and any errors, determines the next protocol action to take (join, sync, heartbeat, rejoin, leave).
nodes.languageNotes: A single large match/decision function implementing the entire consumer group rebalance protocol as an explicit state machine rather than scattered conditionals.

nodes.name: primitive.rs
nodes.summary: Type aliases for Kafka wire primitives (e.g., compact strings/arrays, varint-encoded integers) shared across the (de)serializer implementations.

nodes.name: resource.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the ACL resource-pattern-type enum (literal, prefixed, match, any) used when matching Kafka resources against ACL rules.

nodes.name: Pattern
nodes.summary: Enum of ACL resource-pattern-matching types (Literal, Prefixed, Match, Any, Unknown) used when matching Kafka resources against ACL rules.

nodes.name: ser.rs
nodes.summary: Custom serde Serializer implementation for the Kafka wire format, encoding primitives, flexible/compact fields, and record batches directly to byte buffers, mirroring de.rs's decoder.

nodes.name: Kind
nodes.summary: Internal marker enum distinguishing which serde value kind (field, sequence element, map key) is currently being encoded.

nodes.name: Container
nodes.summary: Tracks the message/type name context of the value currently being serialized, used for flexible-version field lookups.

nodes.name: FieldLookup
nodes.summary: Helper resolving a struct field's wire metadata (tag, flexible/compact flag) by field name during encoding.

nodes.name: Meta
nodes.summary: Per-field/version metadata consulted while encoding a struct field.

nodes.name: Encoder
nodes.summary: Top-level serde Serializer over a byte buffer implementing the Kafka wire format, dispatching to per-type encode routines and tracking flexible/nullable/sequence context.

nodes.name: RecordBatchEncoder
nodes.summary: Serializer specialized for encoding a Kafka RecordBatch (varint-prefixed records with compression/CRC), delegating serde primitive methods to batch-aware encode routines.

nodes.name: serialize_some
nodes.summary: Serializes a Some(value), handling the Kafka wire convention for present optional fields across flexible and non-flexible versions.

nodes.name: serialize_none
nodes.summary: Serializes a None value using the correct null-length sentinel for the field's flexible/fixed encoding.

nodes.name: serialize_i16
nodes.summary: Encodes an i16 field, one of several fixed-width integer encoders that also special-case the tagged-fields count for flexible versions.

nodes.name: serialize_field
nodes.summary: Encodes a single record-batch header field, writing its varint-prefixed key/value bytes.

nodes.name: serialize_str
nodes.summary: Encodes a UTF-8 string field, supporting both plain and compact (flexible-version) length-prefixed encodings.

nodes.name: serialize_bytes
nodes.summary: Encodes a length-prefixed raw byte slice field.

nodes.name: response
nodes.summary: Constructs an Encoder scoped to encoding a response-side message for the given API key and version.

nodes.name: is_flexible
nodes.summary: Determines whether the field currently being encoded uses the flexible (compact/tagged-fields) wire format for its API version.

nodes.name: group.rs
nodes.summary: Declares the Coordinator trait for Kafka consumer-group protocol operations (join, sync, heartbeat, leave, offset commit/fetch) and the OffsetCommit request payload type.

nodes.name: OffsetCommit
nodes.summary: Request payload for a Kafka OffsetCommit call: group id, generation/member epoch, member id, optional group instance id, retention time, and per-topic offsets.

nodes.name: Coordinator
nodes.summary: Trait defining the Kafka consumer-group coordinator contract: join, sync, heartbeat, leave, and offset commit/fetch operations that any group-coordination backend must implement.

nodes.name: avro.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Avro schema backend: parses Avro schemas for key/value/meta, validates and decodes Kafka records against them, converts between Avro binary, JSON, and Kafka record representations, and generates sample records.

nodes.name: json.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the JSON Schema backend for topic validation, compiling jsonschema validators for key/value payloads and converting validated batches to Kafka records and JSON values.

nodes.name: proto.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the Protocol Buffers schema backend: builds file descriptors from proto definitions, encodes/decodes/validates Kafka messages as protobuf, and generates randomized sample messages via a Rhai scripting engine for field customization.
nodes.languageNotes: Embeds the Rhai scripting engine to let field generators be customized per-field via user scripts, and uses reflective protobuf descriptors (MessageDescriptor/FieldDescriptorProto) to walk message shapes dynamically.

nodes.name: lake.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the House enum wrapping the Delta, Iceberg, and Parquet data lake implementations behind a common LakeHouse trait, and the LakeHouseType used to distinguish storage formats at runtime.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses cfg feature flags to compile only the lake backends enabled (delta/iceberg/parquet), with House acting as a runtime enum dispatch over async_trait implementations.

nodes.name: MessageKind
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing key, meta, and value message parts within an Avro-schema-backed Kafka record.

nodes.name: Schema
nodes.summary: Avro schema holder for key/value/meta parts; provides parsing from encoded schema bytes, JSON<->Avro conversion, Kafka record validation and decoding, and sample record generation.

nodes.name: from
nodes.summary: Builds an Avro Schema struct (key/value/meta parts and field ids) from a raw schema descriptor, the largest single conversion routine in the file.

nodes.name: field_ids
nodes.summary: Walks an Avro schema's record fields to assign stable numeric field ids used for Arrow/Parquet column mapping.

nodes.name: from_json
nodes.summary: Converts a JSON value into an Avro-encodable value tree according to the target Avro schema, handling unions, records, arrays, and logical types like UUID and timestamps.

nodes.name: json_value
nodes.summary: Converts a decoded Avro value back into a serde_json Value, the inverse of from_json, used when returning schema-backed records as JSON.

nodes.name: as_kafka_record
nodes.summary: Encodes a JSON value into an Avro-serialized Kafka record (key/value/meta) using the Schema's parsed Avro definitions.

nodes.name: as_json_value
nodes.summary: Converts a validated Kafka record batch into its JSON representation using the Avro schema, implementing the AsJsonValue trait.

nodes.name: validate
nodes.summary: Validates a full Kafka record batch against the Avro schema's key and value definitions, implementing the crate Validator trait.

nodes.name: Schema
nodes.summary: JSON Schema holder wrapping compiled jsonschema Validators for key and value payloads, with validation, encoding, and sample-generation methods.

nodes.name: MessageKind
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing key, meta, and value message parts within a JSON-schema-backed Kafka record.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Compiles raw JSON Schema documents (encoded bytes) into jsonschema Validators for the key and value parts of a topic's Schema.

nodes.name: as_kafka_record
nodes.summary: Serializes a JSON value into an encoded Kafka record after validating it against the compiled JSON Schema.

nodes.name: field_ids
nodes.summary: Assigns stable numeric field ids to a JSON Schema's properties for use in Arrow/Parquet column mapping when writing to lake tables.

nodes.name: MessageKind
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing key, meta, and value message parts within a Protobuf-schema-backed Kafka record.

nodes.name: Schema
nodes.summary: Protobuf schema holder wrapping compiled file descriptors; resolves message types, encodes/decodes/validates Kafka records, and generates randomized sample messages.

nodes.name: MessageGenerator
nodes.summary: Wraps a Rhai script engine and a message descriptor to drive randomized/scripted generation of protobuf sample messages.

nodes.name: FieldGeneratorConfiguration
nodes.summary: Enum of per-field-type generator configuration values (Bool, Bytes, numeric types, List, Message, String) used by user-supplied Rhai field generators to customize sample data.

nodes.name: generate_message_kind
nodes.summary: Generates a randomized protobuf message for a given MessageKind (key/meta/value) by walking the message descriptor and producing values per field.

nodes.name: generate
nodes.summary: Populates a dynamic protobuf message instance field-by-field using the Rhai engine and message descriptor, driving randomized message construction.

nodes.name: singular_value
nodes.summary: Produces a randomized single (non-repeated) protobuf field value for a given runtime type, the core value-generation dispatch for all scalar and message field types.

nodes.name: with_field_generator
nodes.summary: Registers a per-field Rhai-scripted generator configuration so a specific protobuf field can produce custom or constrained sample values.

nodes.name: from
nodes.summary: Converts a decoded dynamic protobuf message into a serde_json Value, used when returning protobuf-schema records as JSON.

nodes.name: as_kafka_record
nodes.summary: Encodes a JSON value into a protobuf-serialized Kafka record using the Schema's message descriptors.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Builds a Protobuf Schema from raw file descriptor bytes, constructing the file descriptor set used for message resolution.

nodes.name: make_fd
nodes.summary: Constructs a protobuf FileDescriptor from a raw descriptor proto, resolving dependencies needed to interpret message shapes.

nodes.name: to_json_value
nodes.summary: Decodes an encoded protobuf message and converts it to a JSON value for a specific MessageKind.

nodes.name: House
nodes.summary: Enum wrapping the concrete Delta, Iceberg, and Parquet lake house implementations (or None) behind a single runtime-dispatched type implementing LakeHouse.

nodes.name: LakeHouseType
nodes.summary: Enum identifying which lake table format (Delta, Iceberg, Parquet, or None) is in use, with helper predicates is_delta/is_iceberg/is_parquet.

nodes.name: LakeHouse
nodes.summary: Async trait defining the store/maintain/lake_type operations that every data lake backend (Delta, Iceberg, Parquet) must implement.

nodes.name: store
nodes.summary: Dispatches a validated record batch write to the active lake house backend (Delta/Iceberg/Parquet), recording write metrics via OpenTelemetry.

nodes.name: maintain
nodes.summary: Runs backend-specific table maintenance (e.g., compaction) on the active lake house implementation.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for nisshi-topic: defines the Error type, the Topic enum (Create/Delete/List variants) and its typestate builder entry points, and dispatches Topic::main() to the matching subcommand implementation.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses typestate builders (PhantomData-parameterized Builder<B,N,P>) so that create/delete/list configuration builders only compile once all required fields are set.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Crate-wide error enum aggregating API error codes, client errors, I/O errors, protocol errors, and JSON serialization failures for topic subcommands.

nodes.name: Topic
nodes.summary: Enum representing the three topic subcommands (Create, Delete, List) holding their respective configurations; exposes builder factory methods and an async main() dispatcher.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Async dispatcher that matches on the Topic variant and delegates execution to the matching Create/Delete/List implementation's main() method.

nodes.name: create.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the topic create subcommand: a typestate Builder collects broker URL, topic name, partition count, and configs, then Create::main() sends a CreateTopicsRequest over the Kafka wire protocol and reports the resulting error code.
nodes.languageNotes: Typestate builder pattern (Builder<B, N, P>) enforces at compile time that broker, name, and partitions are all supplied before build() is callable.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Generic typestate builder that incrementally accumulates broker URL, topic name, partition count, and topic configs before producing a Topic::Create configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Fully-specified parameters for a create-topic operation: broker URL, topic name, partition count, and topic-level configuration overrides.

nodes.name: Create
nodes.summary: Executable wrapper around a create-topic Configuration; its async main() connects to the broker and issues the CreateTopicsRequest.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Terminal builder method available once broker, name, and partitions are set; produces a Topic::Create variant wrapping the finished Configuration.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker via ConnectionManager, builds and sends a CreateTopicsRequest with the configured name, partitions, and configs, then maps the response to an ErrorCode.

nodes.name: delete.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the topic delete subcommand: a typestate Builder collects broker URL and topic name, then Delete::main() sends a DeleteTopicsRequest and reports the resulting error code.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the typestate builder pattern used in create.rs, scoped down to the two fields (broker, name) a delete operation needs.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Generic typestate builder that accumulates the broker URL and topic name before producing a Topic::Delete configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Fully-specified parameters for a delete-topic operation: broker URL and topic name.

nodes.name: Delete
nodes.summary: Executable wrapper around a delete-topic Configuration; its async main() connects to the broker and issues the DeleteTopicsRequest.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker via ConnectionManager, builds and sends a DeleteTopicsRequest using a null topic id and the configured topic name, then maps the response to an ErrorCode.

nodes.name: list.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the topic list subcommand: a typestate Builder collects the broker URL, then List::main() sends a MetadataRequest and prints the resulting topic metadata as JSON.
nodes.languageNotes: Mirrors the typestate builder pattern used in create.rs and delete.rs, scoped to the single broker field a list operation needs.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Generic typestate builder that accumulates the broker URL before producing a Topic::List configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Fully-specified parameters for a list-topics operation, holding only the broker URL to connect to.

nodes.name: List
nodes.summary: Executable wrapper around a list-topics Configuration; its async main() connects to the broker and issues the MetadataRequest.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker via ConnectionManager, sends a MetadataRequest with topic discovery disabled, then serializes and prints the returned topic list as JSON.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for the nisshi-cat CLI: defines the shared Error type, the Cat enum that dispatches between produce and consume subcommands, and the Builder facade used to start each subcommand.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses thiserror with #[from] variants to aggregate client, protocol, schema, IO, and JSON errors into a single Error enum.

nodes.name: consume.rs
nodes.summary: Implements the consume subcommand: builds a Kafka client, issues Metadata and Fetch requests for a configured topic/partition, decodes the returned record batches, and writes each record (optionally schema-validated as JSON) as a line to stdout.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Unified error enum aggregating client, protocol, schema-registry, IO, lines-codec, and JSON errors surfaced by the cat CLI subcommands.

nodes.name: Cat
nodes.summary: Enum representing either a Produce or Consume subcommand configuration, with a main() method that dispatches execution to the selected variant.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Zero-sized builder facade exposing produce() and consume() entry points that hand off to the respective subcommand builders.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Dispatches Cat execution by converting the boxed configuration into a Produce or Consume instance via try_from and awaiting its main() method.

nodes.name: Builder
nodes.summary: Builder collecting broker, topic, partition, schema registry, and fetch-tuning fields before constructing a consume Configuration.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.summary: Immutable configuration for a consume operation, capturing broker, topic, partition, fetch tuning parameters, and an optional schema registry URL.

nodes.name: Consume
nodes.summary: Holds the resolved Configuration plus an optional schema-registry client and implements the consume workflow: metadata lookup, fetch, batch decode, and optional schema-validated JSON output.

nodes.name: try_from
nodes.summary: Converts a consume Configuration into a Consume instance, eagerly resolving an optional schema-registry URL into a Registry client.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to the broker, issues Metadata and Fetch requests for the configured topic/partition, decodes the returned Kafka record batches, and writes each record (optionally schema-validated as JSON) as a line to stdout.

nodes.name: error.rs
nodes.summary: Defines the shared Error enum for nisshi-model, with constructors and From conversions from io, UTF-8, integer/bool parsing, JSON, and syn errors so the JSON message-descriptor parser can surface failures through a single error type.

nodes.name: lib.rs
nodes.summary: Crate root for nisshi-model: models Apache Kafka's JSON message protocol descriptors (Kind, Field, Message, Version, VersionRange, Listener, MessageKind, CommonStruct, and *Meta types) and parses them from raw JSON via TryFrom<&Wv>, feeding nisshi-sans-io's build.rs code generator.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses quote::ToTokens implementations extensively so the parsed model can re-emit itself as Rust syntax (via syn::parse_str::<Expr>) for the downstream proc-macro-style code generator.

nodes.name: wv.rs
nodes.summary: Provides Wv, a thin wrapper around serde_json::Value, plus the As/AsOption traits that pull typed fields (bools, sized integers, strings, arrays, VersionRange) out of raw Kafka descriptor JSON with descriptive parse errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Heavy use of generic trait implementations (As<'a, T> / AsOption<'a, T>) per target type to give ergonomic, type-checked accessors over an untyped serde_json::Value.

nodes.name: Error
nodes.summary: Enum of all nisshi-model failure modes (message parsing, JSON, IO, UTF-8, integer/bool conversion, syn parsing, stack/field lookup errors) with custom() helpers and From impls for ergonomic '?' propagation.

nodes.name: type_mapping
nodes.summary: Maps a Kafka descriptor type name (e.g. int8, string, records) to the corresponding Rust type expression string, recursing for sequence ([]T) types.

nodes.name: is_reserved_keyword
nodes.summary: Checks a field name against the full list of Rust reserved keywords so Field::ident() knows when to emit a raw identifier (r#keyword).

nodes.name: Kind
nodes.summary: Wraps a Kafka field's raw type string (e.g. 'int32', '[]string') and exposes queries (is_sequence, is_primitive, is_float, kind_of_sequence) plus Rust type-name generation used by the code generator.

nodes.name: Listener
nodes.summary: Enum of Kafka listener types (ZkBroker, Broker, Controller) a message applies to, parsed from the descriptor's 'listeners' array.

nodes.name: MessageKind
nodes.summary: Enum distinguishing whether a parsed Kafka message descriptor is a Request or Response.

nodes.name: VersionRange
nodes.summary: Represents a Kafka API version range (e.g. '3+', '0-4') with a start/end pair, parsed via a regex in from_str and queried with within() to check version applicability.

nodes.name: Version
nodes.summary: Aggregates a message's valid, deprecated, and flexible VersionRanges, parsed from the descriptor's validVersions/deprecatedVersions/flexibleVersions fields.

nodes.name: Field
nodes.summary: Core recursive data model for a single Kafka message field: name, Kind, versions, nullability, tag/tagged status, entity type, default, and nested sub-fields, parsed from JSON via TryFrom<&Wv>.

nodes.name: Message
nodes.summary: Top-level parsed representation of one Kafka request/response JSON descriptor: apiKey, kind, name, version, listeners, fields, and any common structs, with helpers (has_records, has_tags, has_float, wrapper_new_type) used by the generator.

nodes.name: CommonStruct
nodes.summary: Represents a named, reusable struct definition declared in a message descriptor's 'commonStructs' section, with its own field list.

nodes.name: HeaderMeta
nodes.summary: Lightweight metadata struct (name, valid version, flexible flag, fields) describing a Kafka request/response header for code generation.

nodes.name: MessageMeta
nodes.summary: Generator-facing metadata view of a Message (name, api_key, version, message_kind, fields) exposing is_flexible/structures/field helpers used when emitting generated Rust types.

nodes.name: FieldMeta
nodes.summary: Generator-facing metadata view of a Field (version, nullable, kind, tag, tagged, nested fields) with is_nullable/is_mandatory/is_structure/structures helpers for driving code generation.

nodes.name: KindMeta
nodes.summary: Generator-facing metadata view over Kind exposing name/is_sequence/is_primitive/is_string/is_records/kind_of_sequence queries used while emitting generated types.

nodes.name: Wv
nodes.summary: Tuple struct wrapping a borrowed serde_json::Value; the entry point every Kafka descriptor parser (Field, Message, Listener, etc.) uses to read typed fields off raw JSON.

nodes.name: As
nodes.summary: Trait defining as_a(&self, name) -> Result<T, Error>, implemented for bool/u64/u32/u16/i64/i16/String/&[Value]/VersionRange to fetch a mandatory typed field from a Wv.

nodes.name: AsOption
nodes.summary: Trait defining as_option(&self, name) -> Result<Option<T>, Error>, implemented per type to fetch an optional typed field from a Wv, returning None when the JSON key is absent or null.

nodes.name: about.toml
nodes.summary: cargo-about license-clarification configuration resolving ambiguous or non-standard licenses for dependencies such as object_store, linux-raw-sys, deadpool-postgres, and libbz2-rs-sys.

nodes.name: codebook.toml
nodes.summary: Codebook spell-checker configuration for the repository, tuning dictionary behavior for the codebase's technical vocabulary.

nodes.name: command-scram-256.properties
nodes.summary: Sample Kafka client properties file for connecting over SASL_PLAINTEXT using SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication.

nodes.name: command-scram-512.properties
nodes.summary: Sample Kafka client properties file for connecting over SASL_PLAINTEXT using SCRAM-SHA-512 authentication.

nodes.name: command.properties
nodes.summary: Minimal Kafka client properties selecting the SASL_PLAINTEXT security protocol with the SCRAM-SHA-256 mechanism, likely a default/base config for command-line testing.

nodes.name: duckdb-init.sql
nodes.summary: DuckDB initialization script that installs/loads the httpfs extension and configures S3 (MinIO) connection settings and credentials for querying Iceberg/Delta lake tables locally.

nodes.summary: Template environment file listing configurable variables for Docker Compose and the broker (cluster ID, listener URLs, AWS/MinIO credentials, storage engine, Iceberg catalog settings), meant to be copied to `.env`.

nodes.summary: Implementation plan for adding the remaining Kafka consumer partition assignors (RoundRobin, Uniform/Sticky, CooperativeSticky), covering assignor semantics, a step-by-step refactor/implementation plan, and a matching test plan.

nodes.name: rustfmt.toml
nodes.summary: rustfmt configuration defining the project's code formatting rules, enforced by `just fmt` in CI.

nodes.summary: Recorded PostgreSQL schema migration diff between Nisshi versions 0.5.0 and 0.6.0, listing the sequence of ALTER TABLE constraint drops and other DDL statements applied to the storage schema.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Nisshi is a stateless, Apache Kafka-compatible broker written in Rust, with pluggable storage backends (PostgreSQL, libSQL, S3, SlateDB, memory) and optional Iceberg and Delta Lake output for schema-backed topics. The README gives the pitch and quick start; the rest of the tour follows a request from the binary down to storage.

tour.title: The Cargo Workspace
tour.description: The root manifest ties the 15-plus member crates together and fixes shared dependency versions, feature flags and lint policy (unsafe code is forbidden). Reading it first gives you the map of crates that every later step refers to, including the storage split into nisshi-storage, nisshi-storage-sql, nisshi-storage-slatedb, nisshi-storage-dynostore and nisshi-storage-null.

tour.title: The Binary and CLI Dispatch
tour.description: A single nisshi binary dispatches to subcommands (broker by default, plus cat, topic, generator, perf and proxy). The binary is deliberately thin; argument parsing lives in the clap-based nisshi-cli crate, which turns flags and environment into the configuration used in the next steps.
tour.languageLesson: Rust binaries keep main small and push logic into library crates. That makes the logic testable, since integration tests can call library code directly without spawning a process.

tour.title: Wire Protocol Codegen
tour.description: nisshi-sans-io holds the Kafka wire protocol as pure serde types with no I/O ('sans-I/O'). Its build.rs reads the upstream Kafka JSON message descriptors and generates typed request and response structs, which the service and broker layers in the next steps consume. Never edit the generated output by hand.
tour.languageLesson: A Cargo build.rs script runs at compile time and can emit Rust source into OUT_DIR. It keeps ~185 protocol messages in sync with upstream Kafka without hand-written boilerplate.

tour.title: Network Service Layers
tour.description: nisshi-service builds the network stack from rama Layers and Services: TCP bytes become Kafka frames, frames are routed to typed handlers, and responses flow back out. The same composition serves the broker, proxy and client. Per-request ambient data travels in the Extensions bag carried inside the input types you saw in Step 4.
tour.languageLesson: Tower-style Layer/Service composition wraps one service in another to add behavior. Handlers stay small and the pipeline is assembled from reusable parts.

tour.title: The Generic Broker
tour.description: Broker<G, S> is generic over a group Coordinator and a Storage implementation, so the same Kafka API handlers run against any backend. The coordinator handles consumer group membership and offsets, while the service module wires handlers into the Step 5 pipeline. Node ID is fixed at 111 because the design is stateless and single-node.
tour.languageLesson: Rust generics with trait bounds give compile-time dispatch: Broker<G, S> is monomorphized per concrete coordinator and storage pair, with no dynamic dispatch cost in the handlers.

tour.title: Storage Abstraction
tour.description: nisshi-storage defines the Storage trait the broker depends on, and a StorageContainer enum that dispatches at runtime to whichever backend the URL scheme selected. A channel-based request service lets storage run behind a queue, and its methods all follow one macro pattern. This is the seam where Step 6's generic parameter S gets filled in.

tour.title: SQL Backends and Schema
tour.description: nisshi-storage-sql implements Storage for PostgreSQL and libSQL on a shared set of queries. The numbered DDL files define the tables behind the model: cluster, topic, topition (topic partition), consumer group and offsets, and records. Backend-specific modules adapt the shared SQL to each database driver.
tour.languageLesson: Numbered DDL files (010-, 020-, 030-) apply in lexical order, so foreign-key targets like cluster are created before tables that reference them such as topition.

tour.title: Object Store and KV Backends
tour.description: The other backends take different approaches. Dynostore targets S3-compatible and in-memory object stores, SlateDB provides an embedded LSM key-value engine, and the null backend discards data for benchmarking and tests. All plug into the same Storage trait from Step 7, so the broker never knows which is in use.

tour.title: Schema Registry
tour.description: nisshi-schema validates and registers Avro, JSON Schema and Protobuf schemas for topics. Producers send records that are checked against the registered schema, which is the prerequisite for turning topics into typed lake tables. Sample schemas under etc/schema and the test fixtures show the formats in use.
tour.languageLesson: Protobuf field numbers are permanent identifiers on the wire. Schema evolution (see the migrate-00N.proto fixtures) is safe only when you add fields rather than renumber or reuse them.

tour.title: Writing to the Data Lake
tour.description: With a schema in hand, the lake module converts records to Parquet and writes them as Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake tables. Features gate each format, so a default build stays small. This is what makes a schema-backed Kafka topic queryable by analytics engines.

tour.title: Proxy and Authentication
tour.description: nisshi-proxy lets the same service layers front another Kafka cluster, and nisshi-auth adds SASL handshakes and SCRAM authentication to connections. Both reuse the Step 5 pipeline, which shows how composable layers extend behavior without touching the broker.

tour.title: Containers and Local Stack
tour.description: The Dockerfile builds a minimal runtime image, and compose.yaml brings up the local environment the integration tests depend on: PostgreSQL, MinIO, the lakehouse catalog, and Grafana, Prometheus and Jaeger for observability. The PostgreSQL initdb DDL seeds the database from Step 8.
tour.languageLesson: Docker multi-stage builds separate the toolchain-heavy build stage from a small final image, which here ends up as a scratch-based runtime.

tour.title: CI/CD Pipeline
tour.description: The CI workflow gates every change on formatting, clippy, docs, tests against PostgreSQL, and client compatibility checks with librdkafka and franz-go. A broader feature and storage matrix runs at merge-queue time, and a release workflow publishes artifacts. It is the final proof that every backend and the Kafka client suites still work.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions jobs run in parallel by default, and a single aggregate gate job (ci-gate) lets branch protection require one check instead of many.
